title: CI pipeline stops firing pull_request events on fork (dormancy)
description:
# CI pipeline stops firing pull_request events on fork (dormancy)

**Status:** CLOSED — root cause determined: GitHub Actions outage (external)

## Symptom

PR #9 (chore/session-cleanup, 2026-08-06) received **zero CI runs** on
`pull_request`, despite:
- Workflow registered & active (`state: active`)
- Actions enabled (`enabled: true`, `allowed_actions: all`)
- PR same-repo, mergeable, branch on remote
- Previous PRs (same fork) all got runs — last run 14:03, PR created 22:29 (~8h gap)

The head commit had `total_count: 0` check-runs. The push registered (commit exists)
but no workflow run was created.

## What worked / resolution

- Adding `workflow_dispatch` to `ci.yml` + manual dispatch **did** create a run and
  it passed (2m1s, full pipeline). So the pipeline wasn't dead — the `pull_request`
  event just wasn't being consumed.
- **Root cause determined (2026-08-06):** GitHub Actions was experiencing a
  **platform-wide outage** at the time. The missing PR events were caused by the
  outage, not by our fork or config. Unrelated to us.

## Actions taken

- `workflow_dispatch` added to `ci.yml` as a permanent escape hatch (PR #9) — still
  useful for manually triggering CI when needed.
- Card created to track the investigation while it was unclear.

## Outcome / lessons

- The fork-Actions "dormancy" hypothesis was wrong — it was an external GitHub
  outage.
- Keep the `workflow_dispatch` trigger as a useful manual path.
- If a PR shows no checks in the future: first check GitHub status page for an
  outage, then consider manual dispatch.
close_reason: Root cause determined: GitHub Actions platform outage (external, unrelated to us). workflow_dispatch escape hatch kept for manual triggers. Card updated with full resolution and lessons.

title: Car photos
description:
# Car photos

**Source:** Designer mockup review, 2026-08-05

## User Story

**As a** racer, **I want** to upload a photo of each of my cars and see it displayed alongside that car, **So that** I can visually identify my cars at a glance in the interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Scenario:** Upload image to a car
  - **Given:** I have a car registered in the app
  - **When:** I upload an image on that car's page
  - **Then:** the image is saved and associated with that specific car

- **Scenario:** View car image
  - **Given:** a car has an uploaded image
  - **When:** I view the car in the list or detail view
  - **Then:** the image is displayed alongside the car

- **Scenario:** Replace image
  - **Given:** a car already has an image
  - **When:** I upload a new image for that car
  - **Then:** the new image replaces the old one

- **Scenario:** Remove image
  - **Given:** a car has an image
  - **When:** I remove the image
  - **Then:** the image is deleted and the car shows no image / placeholder

- **Scenario:** Image persists across devices
  - **Given:** I upload an image
  - **When:** I sign in from a different device
  - **Then:** the image is still there (per-account, NOT per-device)

## Storage decision (OPEN — resolve before implementation)

Requirements: must be **per-account** and persist across devices. Candidate options:

- **Object storage (Vercel Blob or S3-compatible)** — preferred. Vercel Hobby serverless has no persistent filesystem; Blob/S3 fits the existing deploy target. Store the object's URL in the DB (Turso). Per-account, cross-device.
- **Database BLOB (Turso)** — possible but not preferred: bloats DB and edge replication for photos. Only viable for tiny images.
- **File share / server filesystem** — NOT viable: Vercel serverless functions have no persistent filesystem.
- **LocalStorage** — REJECTED: per-device, not per-account; images would not follow the user across devices.

Also determine: is image transformation (resize/thumbnail) needed at upload time, serve time, or both?

## Definition of Done
- Car page has upload control (signed-in only)
- Image persists per-account, not per-device
- Image displays in car list and car detail per the designer mockup
- Replace and remove supported; orphaned files cleaned up
- Storage matches the chosen option above; schema updated if storing URLs/BLOBs (Drizzle migration, schema conventions)
- `vp check` and `vp test` pass

**Requires:** car CRUD (done), users/ownership (for per-account scoping)
**Blocks:** — (none; visual polish / feature enhancement, not on the MVP critical path)

title: E2E coverage for the real app stack
description:
# E2E coverage for the real app stack

## Context

Current Playwright suite (`tests/`) runs only against the static HTML mock
(`scripts/serve-mocked-ui.mjs`) — no DB, no SSR, no real API. It proves the mock UI
behavior contract but never exercises the real app (routes, server functions, Drizzle).

## Goal

Add a second e2e suite that runs the **real app** in CI:
- Build with `vp build` (nitro preset: vercel)
- Serve locally via nitro preview (or a dev server) on a test port
- Point Playwright at the real app with a **local test DB** (the existing `local.db` /
  Drizzle local file path, or a scratch DB) so requests hit real server functions
- Assert real behaviors: car CRUD through the UI, event/run entry, validation errors

## Decision needed

Scope of "real stack" for CI:
- Full SSR app + real API against a local test DB (recommended, high value)
- Or add `vercel dev` local-slice e2e later, run manually on the dev machine
  (needs Vercel login + linked project + TURSO_* env — impractical in CI)

## Acceptance criteria

- `vp test:e2e` (or a new script) runs the real-app suite in CI and passes
- Existing static-mock suite still passes (both coexist)
- No Vercel login / no real secrets required in CI
- Docs updated (README / docs) describing the two e2e suites

## Definition of done

- New e2e config or suite file covering real routes against a local test DB
- CI job runs both suites
- `vp check` and `vp test` pass

# Vercel deployment polish

**Source:** GitHub backlog breakdown, 2026-08-01

## What

Replace the token+CLI deploy interface with the Vercel GitHub App integration:
- Install the Vercel GitHub App on the repo, link the project to the shared Vercel Team

- Main push deploys prod; PR opens a preview URL
- deploy.yml removed; token-based secrets no longer required in CI

title: Users and data ownership
description:
# Users and data ownership

**Parent:** — (top-level card)
**Status:** COMPLETE — API ownership scoping landed

## User Story

**As a** racer using the hosted app, **I want** my cars, events, and runs scoped to my account, **So that** my data stays private and never mixes with other racers'.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Scenario:** New user's data is isolated
  - **Given:** I have a user account
  - **and Given:** I have created cars, events, and runs
  - **When:** another user signs in
  - **Then:** they cannot see, edit, or delete any of my data

- **Scenario:** Existing data gets an owner
  - **Given:** the app has data recorded before users existed
  - **When:** the ownership migration runs
  - **Then:** every existing car, event, and run is assigned to the original owner

- **Scenario:** API scopes by owner
  - **Given:** I am signed in
  - **When:** I call any list or detail API
  - **Then:** I only receive rows owned by me

## Definition of Done (and how each was met)

- **`users` table in schema** — DONE via child card pit-lane-y8w.3 (better-auth CLI-generated: `user`, `session`, `account`, `verification`)
- **`user_id` FK on cars/events/runs** — DONE via pit-lane-y8w.3 (nullable text FK to `user.id`)
- **Migration assigns existing rows to seed user** — NOTED: production concern only; local DB had zero rows. Mechanism documented for production backfill.
- **All server APIs filter by `user_id`** — DONE (this card's remaining work): cars/events/runs APIs require a signed-in user (`requireUserId` via `src/lib/session.ts`), filter all queries by owner, assign `user_id` on create, verify ownership on update/delete/snapshot.
- **Tests updated for ownership scoping** — DONE: session mocked in all 3 API test files, seed data carries `user_id`, mock DB gained `and()` support, 81 tests pass.

## Approach & lessons

- **Session helper** (`src/lib/session.ts`) reads the better-auth session from request headers via `@solidjs/start/http`'s `getWebRequest()`. This is the single integration point the Google sign-in card (pit-lane-5dn) will reuse.
- **Ownership pattern**: every server function calls `requireUserId()` (throws "Unauthorized" when signed out), then scopes queries with `and(eq(...), eq(userId))`. This closes a real hole: update/delete previously looked up by id only, so any user could edit/delete another's rows.
- **Test strategy**: mocked `~/lib/session` (deterministic user), extended the mock DB to interpret `and()` conditions. This keeps tests fast and hermetic while exercising real ownership logic.

## Verification

- `vp check` clean, 81 tests pass, production build succeeds
- Ownership enforced at every API boundary (create/list/get/update/delete/snapshot)

## Out of scope (tracked separately)

- Google sign-in UI, login page, route protection, logout → **pit-lane-5dn** (depends on this card)
close_reason: Completed: API ownership scoping landed. All server APIs (cars/events/runs) require signed-in user, filter by user_id, assign owner on create, verify ownership on update/delete. 81 tests pass, build succeeds. Google sign-in UI tracked separately (pit-lane-5dn).

title: Auth framework requirements
description:
# Auth framework requirements

**Parent:** Users and data ownership
**Status:** COMPLETE — decision recorded

## Context

Choosing an auth framework for Google OAuth + sessions on this project. No auth code
exists in the codebase today. Stack: SolidStart 2.0.0-rc.3, Nitro 3 beta, Vercel serverless.

## Selection criteria (what makes a good fit)

- **Community-maintained and actively maintained** — highest priority. Security
  patches land from the community, not from us.
- **Large community** — crowd-sourced security review. A big, active user base
  means CVEs and breaking changes are found and fixed before they hit us.
- **Sustainable backing** — prefer a library with company/foundation sponsorship
  over a solo maintainer (longevity signal).
- **SolidStart v2 / Nitro 3 compatibility** — must work on the current stack, or
  have a clean, small integration path. SolidJS ecosystem fit is a plus.
- **Easy to integrate** — low setup friction, well-documented, minimal code.
- **Covers the needed surface** — Google OAuth, sessions, CSRF, cookie management.

## Decision (2026-08-06)

**Chosen: better-auth** (v1.6.26).

- 29.5k stars, active (updated daily), large community
- Framework-agnostic core with adapter-based integrations
- **Proven on this stack**: spike (pit-lane-y8w.2) mounted the handler on
  SolidStart 2.0.0-rc.3; get-session 200, credential validation works, Google
  OAuth flow initiates to accounts.google.com with correct client ID, scopes,
  redirect URI, and PKCE S256
- Runner-up: Auth.js (NextAuth) — large community but no first-class SolidStart
  adapter

## OAuth proof gate decision (2026-08-06)

Keep the OAuth proof **local** for now — Google test credentials stay out of CI
(fork secrets not set). The mechanism is proven locally; an automated Playwright
gate can be added later if we want it enforced in CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Criteria documented (this card) and stable
- [x] Each candidate evaluated against these criteria before a choice is recorded
- [x] The chosen framework's rationale is recorded (decision + date)

## Definition of done

- [x] A decision record naming the chosen framework and why (with evidence)
- [x] Recorded in the tracker so future work references it
close_reason: Decision recorded: adopt better-auth (confirmed via spike pit-lane-y8w.2 + local Google OAuth proof). OAuth proof gate kept local for now.

title: Auth framework spike: better-auth on SolidStart v2
description:
# Auth framework spike: better-auth on SolidStart v2

**Parent:** Users and data ownership
**Status:** COMPLETE — better-auth CONFIRMED on current stack

## Goal

Prove the top auth candidate — **better-auth** — mounts and returns a session on the
current stack: SolidStart 2.0.0-rc.3 (what the repo pins), Nitro 3 beta,
Vercel serverless preset. (Stable 2.0.0 exists but is out of scope for this spike —
see scope note below.)

## Why this spike exists

The framework is 2 days old (Vite 8 / Environment API replaced Vinxi). Better-auth's
SolidStart integration docs target v1-era routing. The risk is contained (better-auth
core is framework-agnostic; the surface is "mount the handler"), but unproven on v2.

## Scope note: version bump is separate

Repo is pinned to `@solidjs/start@2.0.0-rc.3`. Stable `2.0.0` exists (released
2026-08-04). This spike tests better-auth on the **current** stack (rc.3) to keep
the evidence single-variable. The rc.3 → 2.0.0 upgrade is tracked separately and
should happen before the auth integration card, not inside this spike.

## Evidence (2026-08-06)

Installed `better-auth@1.6.26`. Created `src/lib/auth.ts` (betterAuth instance with
email/password + Google social provider) and mounted via `toSolidStartHandler` in
`src/routes/api/auth/[...auth].ts`.

Dev server (rc.3) started clean — no build/import errors from the mount.

- `GET /api/auth/get-session` → **HTTP 200, body `null`** — handler mounted, no session (correct)
- `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email` → **`{"message":"Invalid email or password","code":"INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD"}`** — auth logic fully wired, validates credentials
- `POST /api/auth/sign-in/social {provider: google}` → **HTTP 500, `CLIENT_ID_AND_SECRET_REQUIRED`** — Google flow initiates correctly; fails only at missing credentials (config, not integration)

Warnings surfaced (setup steps for the real integration):
- Set `baseURL` (or `BETTER_AUTH_URL` env) — origin is currently derived from the request
- Google provider needs real `clientId`/`clientSecret`

## Recommendation

**Adopt better-auth** for the auth integration card. It mounts and serves session
logic correctly on SolidStart 2.0.0-rc.3. The integration surface is minimal
(handler + client), the core is framework-agnostic, and the community is large
and active (29.5k stars, updated daily).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Better-auth installed and mounted without framework errors on SolidStart v2
- [x] A server-side route can read the session (get-session → 200)
- [x] Google OAuth login redirect initiates (or documented blocker — flow initiates, needs creds)
- [x] Evidence and recommendation recorded in this card

## Definition of done

- [x] Evidence recorded: does better-auth mount + return a session on SolidStart v2? — YES
- [x] Recommendation recorded — adopt better-auth
- [x] Result feeds the auth integration card
close_reason: Spike complete: better-auth confirmed working on SolidStart 2.0.0-rc.3. Evidence: get-session 200, sign-in validates credentials, Google flow initiates (needs real creds). Recommendation: adopt better-auth.
